newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end sharply down on bank selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end sharply down on bank selling.

text.p: Shanghai A and B shares ended sharply down on Wednesday mainly due to state banks offsetting their positions in the market, traders said.
Beijing last week ordered state banks to stop trading on the stock markets and wind up their positions within 10 days to effectively cut bank money from flowing into the markets.

The foreign currency B share index shed 2.524 points or 2.96 percent to 82.797 points on volume of 17.8 million shares worth $11.9 million. The domestic A share index lost 22.123 points or 1.71 percent to 1,273.782 points on volume of 336.7 million shares worth 4.5 billion yuan.
"State banks were seen offsetting positions on the A share market, pushing down the A index," one A share tradde said.
"Falls on the A market depressed sentiment on the B share market," said a B share trader. "Domestic investors sold on the B share market, making the B share index fall."
The A share index hit an intra-day low of 1,225.722 points late in the morning session and the B index hit a low of 82.576 points in late afternoon trading.
Speculative buying in the last few minutes of trading pushed the indices off their lows at the close, traders said.

"Market sentiment is very weak though the indices regained part of the lost ground late in trading," said a second trader. "There is still great potential for the indices to continue to fall in the next few days if there is no major positive news."

A commentary by the official Financial Times based in Beijing said the central government would continue to take measures to cool down stock trading and would not support the stock markets because of China's takeover of Hong Kong in July.
"The commentary has made investors firmly believe the recent market rumours will be confirmed eventually," a Shanghai stock analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
Traders said there were persistant rumours saying Beijing would shortly announce new measures to cool down stock trading, including punishment of major brokerages for irregularities.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co was the biggest B share loser with traders saying its price/earnings ratio was at a very high level. It lost $0.046 or 8.88 percent to $0.472 on volume of 206,000 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power Co was the most actively traded B share on volume of 3.1 million shares, falling $0.024 or 2.79 percent to $0.836 on institutional liquidation.
On the A share market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index closed down 110.643 points or 2.80 percent to 3,846.388 points.
Shanghai Jiafeng Co was the worst performer on institutional liquidation, plunging 0.56 yuan to close at a 10-percent limit-down level of 5.02 yuan on volume of 239,600 shares.
